entities.summary:
The Austro-Turkish War of 1788–1791 was a pivotal military conflict between the Habsburg Monarchy and the Ottoman Empire, fought in the Military Frontier region between 1788 and 1791. This war marked a significant escalation of the long-standing struggle between the two empires, with the Habsburgs seeking to expand their territories in Southeastern Europe and the Ottomans determined to maintain their control over the region.

The war began on February 1, 1788, with the Habsburgs launching a series of military campaigns against Ottoman-held territories. The conflict saw significant battles, including the Siege of Buda and the Battle of Karánsebes, as both sides suffered heavy losses. The war finally ended on August 4, 1791, with the Treaty of Sistova, which marked a decisive victory for the Habsburgs.

The Austro-Turkish War of 1788–1791 had far-reaching consequences, contributing to the decline of the Ottoman Empire and paving the way for the rise of the Habsburgs as a dominant power in Central and Eastern Europe. The war also set the stage for the Napoleonic Wars and the subsequent redrawing of the European map.

One of the most striking legacies of the Austro-Turkish War is the role it played in shaping the modern borders of Southeastern Europe, with the Treaty of Sistova leading to the cession of significant territories from the Ottoman Empire to the Habsburgs.
